notTracked: Most public universities (UC system, Texas, Florida, etc.)

items.tip: Sign in at the admissions office. Both in-person and virtual visits get logged. If you can't visit, attend a regional info session in your city.
ED is the single strongest signal of interest you can send. Reserve it for your true #1 — but if a tracked-DI school is your top choice, ED is non-negotiable.
Most schools track email opens via tracking pixels. When you receive emails, open them — even if you skim. Click at least one link per email.

items.action: Submit a strong, school-specific 'Why Us' essay
items.tip: A generic supplement is a negative DI signal. Reference specific courses, professors, traditions, and clubs.
Both in-person and virtual sessions get logged. Many schools host webinars throughout the year — sign up early and actually attend.

items.action: Connect with your regional admissions officer
items.tip: Email a thoughtful, specific question (not 'what's it like there?'). Ask about a program, course, or research opportunity. Keep it short — 4 sentences max.

items.action: Sign up for the school's mailing list early
items.tip: Sign up junior year, not senior fall. The longer you've been on the list, the stronger the signal.

items.action: Attend a college fair where the school is present
items.tip: Get your barcode scanned and ask one specific question. Follow up with a thank-you email afterward.

items.action: Follow the school on social media
items.tip: Not tracked by admissions, but it keeps you informed about events and deadlines. Don't overdo it.

items.action: Engage with current students or alumni
items.tip: Reach out via LinkedIn or AdmitHub-style chatbots. Not tracked, but it gives you genuine material for your 'Why Us' essay.

items.action: Apply to specific scholarship programs at the school
items.tip: Some scholarships require separate applications. Applying signals serious interest — and may be tracked.
